source.name: sp_GetExternalInventory

assumptions: OPENQUERY linked server functionality mapped to PostgreSQL dblink extension
RemoteWarehouse linked server would need to be configured as a foreign server using postgres_fdw or dblink
ProductCode assumed to be TEXT type (could be VARCHAR or other string type)
AvailableStock assumed to be INTEGER type (could be NUMERIC or BIGINT)
The procedure does not return a result set, only prints/logs the SQL statement
PRINT statement converted to RAISE NOTICE for equivalent logging behavior
NVARCHAR(MAX) converted to TEXT as PostgreSQL standard text type
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't send row counts by default in procedures)

reviewFlags.reason: Linked server configuration must be migrated. PostgreSQL requires either postgres_fdw (for PostgreSQL remote servers) or dblink extension. The remote server connection string, credentials, and foreign data wrapper must be properly configured before this procedure will work.
Column data types in the dblink result set definition are assumed. Verify actual data types from the remote Inventory table and adjust accordingly (e.g., VARCHAR(50), NUMERIC(10,2), etc.).

PRINT behavior differs from RAISE NOTICE. PRINT sends messages to the client immediately in SQL Server, while RAISE NOTICE may be buffered depending on client settings. Consider if this logging is needed in production.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server OPENQUERY requires linked server configuration. PostgreSQL equivalent requires either postgres_fdw (Foreign Data Wrapper) for PostgreSQL servers or dblink extension for ad-hoc connections. Setup and syntax differ significantly.

The procedure builds but does not execute the SQL. If execution is needed in the future, use EXECUTE with dblink or postgres_fdw queries. PostgreSQL dynamic SQL uses EXECUTE command instead of sp_executesql.
PRINT in SQL Server vs RAISE NOTICE in PostgreSQL have different buffering and client handling behaviors. Messages may appear at different times or require different client configuration to display.
PostgreSQL procedures do not send row count messages by default, so SET NOCOUNT ON has no equivalent and is not needed.
